strategy_rationale: Panel structure (jurisdiction x period_id) with strictly non-overlapping train/prediction periods (train ends 2025-05-31, prediction starts 2025-07-31). forward_expanding_time trains strictly on past periods and validates on future blocks, exactly mirroring how the hidden test is later than all training data. GroupKFold over random periods would allow future-period training rows to help predict earlier periods (forward peeking), yielding optimistic OOF. Expanding window avoids this by construction; the last fold's validation block (the 6 most recent training periods) is the closest analogue to the hidden 6-period test.
simulates_hidden_evaluation: Each fold's validation block is 6 consecutive training periods held out as future; the model trains only on periods strictly earlier. The last fold's val block mirrors the hidden test (6 months immediately after training ends). OOF MAE restricted to scoring categories (all_drugs, all_opioids, all_stimulants) matches leaderboard metric.

leakage_risks.action: Target absent from prediction frame by design; no leakage.
period_id is an opaque key; derive only ordinal rank / datetime features (year, month, sin/cos), never use the raw string as a model feature.
Mean shifts from 51.8 (train) to 68.8 (pred). Models should not rely on absolute level; use lags and differences instead.
Mean shifts from 47.0 (train) to 63.7 (pred). Prefer lag/rolling features.
54.6% missing in pred vs 0% in train. Impute with jurisdiction-level median or last known value.
58.0% missing in pred. Same imputation strategy as unemployment_rate.

Train-only sub-categories (benzodiazepine, cocaine, fentanyl, heroin, methamphetamine) absent from prediction frame. Use them as auxiliary signal via cross-category aggregates, not as direct features.

validation_limitations: OOF covers only the last ~30 of 77 training periods (5 folds x 6 periods); earliest periods are always in training and never validated. Distribution shift in gtrends features (train vs pred levels diverge) means even a perfect CV score may underestimate prediction difficulty. Missing covariate data in pred (unemployment_rate 54.6%, labor_force 58%) is not replicated in train, so imputation quality cannot be validated in-sample.
